Stop a service.
Report on a service.

Set where a router sends new connections.
Watch one backend for a while and fail if it misbehaves.
Stop a router listening.
Say which generation the next version of something is, and what it is called.
Say what watching a new version through its stages came to: how many, and in how many nothing reached it.
Read a table's rows as they are taken: each with what it leaves unsaid filled in, and what can be said of them together.

Give a table the rows it starts with: each is added unless the table has a row called what it is called, so that done twice it is the same, and a row somebody changed is left as they have it. It makes the first rows of the table, called what `collection` says.
Say what a bot with a command answers: what the command printed, that it printed nothing, why it could not, or what was said where there is no command.

Say what a card's being moved means for what the card keeps: that it was taken to be worked, sent back (to where cards are worked, or from where work is looked over to any column the board has before that one), finished, or nothing; whether a question on it is settled by the move; and, of one that is finished, which cards wait on it.
Say whether what was said on a card answers what was asked on it: a question is open, and it was not whoever asked who spoke.
Say what a card says while it waits its turn where a limited number are worked at once, and whether what waits is a card of this board at all.
Say whether the cards a card waits on are done, and what follows: what it is to say it waits for, whether that comes off it, and whether whoever would begin it is to be told.
The cards of a board that wait on other cards: those not finished that say so, which is what says they were asked whether they may begin.
Press something a card's column offers on it, as a person would press its button, or take a press back. Who may is what its row says, of whoever applied this.
Say that a card waits where it is for something its column offers to be pressed, once for each time it comes there; nothing, where nothing holds it.
Read what was said on a record since a line of its history, as whoever is to be told it reads it.
Ask a question on a record: said on it by whoever asked, naming with @ each it is put to, so that being named tells them in their inbox. Needs `board:write` for a card, `records:write` for any other.
Say what a change to a record was, in words: the new row, the change to the row or its taking away, which row, of which table, and which of its cells.
Make sure a channel exists. It makes a channel, called what `name` says.
Post a message to a channel.
Take part in a channel as a bot, under a name of its own. It makes a bot, called what `name` says.
Stop taking part in a channel as a bot.
Tell somebody something: a line in their inbox, from the factory's bot.
Have agents of a channel talk things over in its threads, as this says.
Stop a channel offering discussions, as this text offered them.
Write down whose a turn of a discussion was, and how it ended.
Write down how a stretch of a discussion ended, and whom it is told to.
Add a card to a project's board. It makes a card, called what `title` says.

Declare a collection of records for a project: what they are made of, how they are looked at, and where they are kept. It makes a table, called what `name` says. Where `beside` is said, its rows set what something does.
Move a card to another column.
Say of each card that was moved or added with nobody told that it was: for when the daemon has started, and once for each start (asked again, nothing is said).
Change a card's title, details, assignee, labels or the day it is wanted by.
The cards on a project's board.
Read a card.
Add a record to a collection a blueprint declared: a sprint, a release, whatever the project keeps. It makes a row of the table, called what `collection` says.

Keep a record under a number of your choosing, another record's own: added where the table has none of it, and changed to these fields where it has, so that one row stands for one thing and is found again by its id alone.
Change some of a record's fields, leaving the others as they are.
Say something on a record, a card included; it is kept in the record's history and changes nothing of it. Needs `board:write` for a card, `records:write` for any other.
Whether whoever an event says did it holds a scope now. Whoever asks has to hold that scope themselves.
Read a record.
The records of a collection.
Take a record away. What named it goes on saying what it named, and its history is kept.
Attach a file of the record's project to a record, a card included, as a copy: a picture, a video or a log that shows something. Needs what changing the record needs.
Write a library out as web pages that anything can serve: a page a document, with what the pages use beside them. It makes the web pages of the library, called what `collection` says.
Create a project, or adopt an existing directory as one. It makes a project, called what `name` says.
Write a file in a project. It makes a file of the project, called what `path` says.
Read a file in a project.
Notice files that changed outside the system, e.g. after a build.
Bring an agent into the fleet, or update the one with this name. It makes an agent, called what `name` says.
Give an agent a piece of work and wait for it to finish. It reaches, by itself, `std/dispatch` and `std/signin`.
Ask an agent to look at something and choose what happens next. It reaches, by itself, `std/dispatch` and `std/signin`.
Stop an agent: at once, or when it has finished what it has in hand.
Call off what something this started asked of an agent before the daemon last stopped, once it is over without having asked for it again: begun again as the daemon started, nobody waits for it.
Make an item's place to work in, a worktree on a branch of its own, or find the one it has. It makes a place to work in, on a branch of its own, for the item, called what `item` says.
Commit what an agent left uncommitted in an item's place, as the agent's.
Send an item's branch to a remote, as the key the step is handed if it is handed one.
Merge an item's branch into the branch the project's folder has checked out.
Remove an item's worktree, and its branch when its work is somewhere else.
Where an item was worked, and what was changed there against the project's own branch.
The commit a folder of the project is at, where it is in a repository with history.
Give an item the place of another piece of work on it: that worktree and branch become the item's own.
What an item's merge follows up: the earlier items' work it reverts, and those whose files it changes again soon after.

Gather other items' branches, and any branch named, into an item's place, each merged in turn, taking all of them or none. It makes a place on a branch of its own, for the item, holding what is gathered, called what `item` says.
Bring a branch of the project forward to an item's branch where that is a fast-forward, and send it to a remote, as the key the step is handed if it is handed one.
Have the project's branches said as they move (`project.branch.moved`), until the daemon stops. Asked again it changes nothing.
Count one more vote on a card and say whether that settles it: passed, failed, undecided, or not yet.
Say what so many agents of one name are called, and which of those there were are no longer counted.
Say who of a project's agents is there: which of some roles take part in a channel, by name, and how many there are of some roles.
Say what becomes of work that could not be kept: given to whoever did it again, or left for a person.
Say what is kept of something put to an agent a number of times at most: how many rounds there have been, who has it, and whether there may be another.
Say whether a change to something an agent has in hand is news to that agent, and as what.
Say what a turn that came for an item comes to, by what its row says: a round of it begins, or the turn is given back because its round is over or the item is gone.
Say what an item that was said to be due comes to where items are worked: its turn is asked for, it waits on others, or nothing, it having been moved on or taken away.

Say what an item that was said to be due is owed where something is started for each item that comes to a column, by what its row says and what is kept of those begun: it is begun; or nothing, this coming of it having been begun for already, or the item not being in the column.
Say what goes with something started for an item: what it is called, and how often at most it goes round where its row says none.
Say whether an item is still as a round has it, by what its row says of its moves: the round takes it, it is the round's in hand, or it has gone on or been moved by somebody since.
Say what giving an item to an agent came to: it was worked and goes on, its agent asked something in place of working, or there was nobody to give it to and it is left where it is.
Say what a round that ended comes to for whoever asked for it: the item is given again, its place is given back, or nothing more.
Say what becomes of an item's round when somebody moves the item out of the column it is in while in hand: the round is stopped and the item kept as taken out of its agent's hands, or nothing.
Say what an item said to be due a review is owed: a review of it begins, it is left for a person having been sent back as often as is allowed, or nothing.

Say what a verdict on an item comes to: what was done is put with the rest first, the item goes on, it goes back, something is in the way that a person has to put right, it is left for a person, or nothing; and what is said of it where the work is reported.
Say, of a review that is over having said nothing of how it came out, whether its item now waits for a person to review it, and the sentence that says so.
Say, in a sentence for where the work is reported, how much is done at once with the items of a column from now: nothing new for now and why, or so many at a time.
Say what a row that was taken as it now says came to, held against what it said before: whether the items of its column are looked at another way from now, and the sentence that says how.
Say what is wrong with a row that says what is done with the items of a column, each in a sentence: a column it names that is not there, more to look or to approve than there are, nobody to work.
Say which items were left in hand when whatever had them was stopped: those a round was begun for and neither handed on nor said anything of.
Say, in a sentence for where the work is reported, what clearing an item's place came to where something was kept or could not be done; nothing, where there is nothing to say.
Say what the things done with an item where something is begun for each item came to: it goes on, it is left for a person, or nothing.

Say what comes next for an item among the things done with it where it is: the usual ones, with what the rows of a table add, stand in for and take out. Another is run, with what it is handed; the item goes on, goes back or is left for a person; or nothing, it having gone on or been moved.
Say what a command that was run for an item comes to: the item goes on, goes back with what was printed, or is left for a person.
Say what is wrong with the rows of a list of things done with the items of a column, each in a sentence: what a row says that will never be done as it is written.
Say where a command that is run for an item is run: where the item is worked, or in the project's own folder; or that it is not run, the item having no place of its own yet.

Say what is kept of a command that was run for an item, as a row of a table: a run id, the day and the time it began, the item, the commit it ran on, the command, whether it passed and with what code, how long it took and the last of what it printed.

Say what becomes of an item when those who looked at it have said, when the things done with it before anybody looks ended by themselves, or when its looking ended having said nothing: more is done with it where it is, it goes on, it goes back, it is left for a person, it waits for a person to look at it, or nothing; with what is said of it and what is counted.
Say whom something that waits for a person is told to, by the rows that say who is told what, and the sentence that says it.
Say whose turn it is in a discussion, or that it is over: agreed, needing a person, or at its cap.
Say what is said as a stretch of a discussion ends: a line in its thread, whether the person is told and in what words, and what a lead is asked to answer the person with.
Say what an agent's turn came to by the word it ended with, and what goes with it; and the words it may end with, to offer it.
Say what of a chain of rungs is asked before anything is run: whether it has a rung, and which columns a rung names for a card nobody works.
Say who is next for an item that waits on somebody, by the rungs of a chain, and the sentence they are told; and after how long the next rung is to be asked for.
Say what the word an agent that looked at a waiting item decided comes to: back to be worked, a person asked, the next rung told now, the question on it answered, or it waits as it is.

Say the fields of a table of how long cards took on a board with these columns: the card, when it was added and done, the time in all and in each column, how often it was sent back and came to the last column, and who worked it.
Say which of an item's contests is to be done now: one under way, else the oldest waiting, or none.
Say what a contest's contenders come to: the ways of its comparison, the letter a judge picks each by, where each works and how much of its change a judge is shown, or what is wrong with it.
Say the comparisons of their own that contests are counted under, those that name none.
Say what judges who each picked an entry by its letter come to: the entry that won, or that nothing was decided and why.
Read what judges scored each entry, and say what that comes to by the contest's rule: the entry that won, a person to pick, or nothing.
Say what a contest's judges are shown of the entries whose work was kept, by the letters they pick them by, and what each judge is started as.
Say what a council that talks it over came to after a stretch: the entry enough of its seats agreed on, another stretch, or nothing.
Say what becomes of a contest and of each of its entries: something to judge, the entry taken, a person asked, or the contest left.
Say whether every one of several items handed on together was passed, one went back, or some still wait to be looked at.

Say which rows of a project's triggers fire for something that happened, each with the pipeline it runs, the key that run is under and what it is handed of what happened, which is what the pipeline takes.
Say in a sentence why a pipeline asked for by hand was not run: why, or what whoever asked does not hold.
Say which rows of a project's triggers go by the clock, and how, and whether any goes by a branch moving; and of one row whether it goes by `every` or `at` now.
Read the tickets a document lists in its block of them.
Say what a document's tickets came to, once each is a thing with an id: what each waits on, and the document with that written where its block was.
Say, for whoever plans, the rows there already that a plan is to put in order: those named, and with a label every row that carries it and is not done.

Say whether a plan's tickets fit what is there, before anything is made of them: a ticket may be a row there already (`card`, its id) of those the plan was asked to put in order, and waits on places in the list or on rows by id.

Say what every thing of a plan that fits waits on and is part of, once its new tickets have come to rows: those, the rows it named, and the rows it was asked to put in order and did not name, which are taken as they stand.
Say what is to cross between two sides of one thing that is kept in step, each field held against what the two last agreed on: what goes out, what comes in, and what they agree on once that is done.
Say which of the things said on one side have not crossed to the other yet, held against the names of those that have.
Say which of a project's feature flags are past the day they were to go, each with whom it is told to and in what words.

Say whether an item waiting where items are worked may be taken now, or waits behind items worked from there before it that are in hand or handed on and not merged, where the row says the next is taken only once none is.

Read a card's history and say how long it took: from being added to coming to the board's last column, in each column, how often it was sent back, and who worked it, as the row a table of those keeps.
How this device and each device of its fleet stands: what it has free, and how busy it is.

Choose a device with room for a piece of work: of those that have what is asked, the least busy for its size. What it chooses is counted against that device for a short while, so that work asked for together is spread.
Start a blueprint as an instance of its own, or update the one it started before. It makes an instance of its own of the blueprint, called what `blueprint` says.
Stop an instance started with `blueprint.apply`, and what it holds.

Start a comparison whose ways are named by the start, or answer the one there is of that name with the ways asked for added: from now, a start of `of` here whose params say `compared` and `way` goes that way and is measured with it.
End a comparison whose ways are named by the start, in this project: from then a start that names it goes as it is written.

Write a thing down as one of a way's, with nothing started for it, in a comparison whose ways are named by the start in this project: what is said of the thing from then is counted under that way, as the work it goes on with.
Say again the shares of a comparison in this project that shares its things out, with why: from then each way is given its part of what comes next by them.

Say what is true of this profile, the copy of the factory it runs in, for every blueprint here to read as `profile.vars.<name>`. The whole set is replaced. Not for secrets: the values are shown and kept as they are.

Make ready the environments of the project this is applied for, each with no variables yet: one it has already is left as it is. Making one takes what making one by hand does: writing the project, `shell` and `secrets:use`.
Say what a feature flag of the project this is applied for says in one of its environments, or take it away there: the environment's variable of the flag, written with what is said of it.
Work out who of those waiting for a place is given one, after something asked, gave one back or ended.
Put a text together from parts, each said only where it is to be.
Write a copy of this factory to a folder, to start another factory from. The factory is only read. It makes a copy of this factory in the folder, called what `to` says.
Wait for a person to let the run go on, telling whoever may decide in their inbox.
Show some of a project's things in a folder of the side panel, making the folder where it is not there.
Tell the daemon a name it is asked under, so that it answers when it is: the name of whatever was put in front of it.
Stop this factory and have what keeps it running start it again, once nothing else is under way, so that what was installed meanwhile runs from then on.

Write everything this program says of itself into a folder of the project, as pages a library reads: its commands, its language, its actions and events, the blueprints that ship and its guides. It makes the pages of what the program says of itself, in the folder, called what `to` says.
Set the project up with each of these rows that is on: each a blueprint applied for it as whoever applied this, saying what each came to.

description: A blueprint: what exists, what is heard, and what is done. This helps an editor complete and check one as it is written; whether it can be applied is said by checking it.

blueprint.description: Its name, which is how it is applied, called and found again. Lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `/`.

description.description: What it is for, in a sentence: shown where blueprints are listed, and first in what it says in plain words.

durable.description: Whether what an instance is doing is written down as it goes, to be picked up after a restart: true unless said. With `false` it keeps nothing as it goes: what each step did is written once, when the run ends, its state is its own while it lives, and a restart ends it. For work that is short and can simply be done again.

max_parallel.description: How many of its steps may run side by side, 8 unless said: for steps that each take a share of something there is only so much of.

on.description: Handlers: what to do each time something happens while the instance is alive.

on_fail.description: Done when the steps have failed, to tell of it or undo what they began.

on_finish.description: Done when the steps have ended, however they went, after `on_success` or `on_fail`; `run.status` says which.

on_stop.description: Done when the instance is stopped, before what it holds is given back: where it undoes what it set up outside the factory.

on_success.description: Done when the steps have gone well, to tell of it or go on from it.

on_update.description: Done when a running instance takes this text, in place of running its steps again: it carries on from where it is. `was` is what it was before: `was.version`, `was.revision`, `was.state`, `was.params`. If one of these fails, the instance goes back to the text and the state it had.

one_at_a_time.description: Its handlers take turns: one run of any of them at a time, so that one which looks at `state` and then changes it is not overtaken by another. A handler that waits holds up the rest.

outputs.description: What a blueprint that calls this one is given back once its steps have run: names, and what each comes to.

params.description: What an instance is started with. `port: 8080` gives a default; a name with nothing after it must be given.

permissions.description: What it may use, checked before anything runs. With none listed it runs with everything its caller has.

state.description: Durable properties of an instance, with the values they start at. Change them with `do: set`.

steps.description: The work, as a graph of steps. Runs once, when an instance starts.

uses.description: Other blueprints attached to every instance of this one, each started as a child.

version.description: A version of your own choosing, kept with it: what is said of an instance running an earlier text names it, so it goes up when what the text does changes.
